Create a standard curve in a spreadsheet software using the "mean" values (pixel densities) measured from the bands of the Lambda DNA standards in your gel. Chart these values against the known concentrations of the Lambda samples. LibreOffice comes pre-installed with Ubuntu 18.04 and the examples shown in this section use LibreOffice Calc.

steps.title: Prepare 1% agarose gel and load samples
steps.instruction: Pour a 1 % agarose gel. Load 5 µl of your genomic DNA sample onto the gel. Also load 5 µl aliquots of lambda DNA standards at concentrations of 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 µg ml⁻¹ (ng µl⁻¹).

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel for approximately 20 minutes at 100 V. Allow the DNA to migrate 0.5–1.0 cm into the gel; longer runs spread the band more but reduce quantification accuracy.

steps.title: Stain gel with SYBR dye
steps.instruction: Stain the gel for 30 minutes in 1 X SYBR dye (dilute concentrate 1 in 10 000 in the running buffer, either TAE or 0.5 X TBE). Staining can be added to the gel matrix when pouring, but this increases background fluorescence. The staining solution remains stable for at least two weeks and can be reused for several gels.

steps.title: Construct LED transilluminator
steps.instruction: Build a low‑cost light box for gel illumination.

substeps.instruction: Cut a rectangular hole in a cardboard box; the hole should be smaller than the clear plastic sheet that will cover it. In the prototype the hole was 15 × 30 cm.

Cut aluminum strips to serve as heat‑dissipating bases for the LEDs. Make two strips with three LEDs each for the long sides and two strips with two LEDs each for the short sides; drill holes for mounting the LEDs.
Solder each LED to its resistor as shown in the circuit diagram, apply thermal grease to the back of the LEDs, and fix the LEDs to the aluminum strips with small screws.
Poke holes through the cardboard box and secure the aluminum strips with plastic cable ties. Optionally install a small fan for airflow.
Line the bottom of the box with black paper to reduce reflections.
Close the box and place a clear plastic (polycarbonate or equivalent) sheet over the top to cover the hole.

steps.title: Set up camera and computer
steps.instruction: Turn on the computer and the digital camera. Screw the orange Tiffen 55 mM 21 filter onto the camera lens. Set the camera to save RAW images. Connect the camera to the computer with a mini‑USB cable (or appropriate cable) so that a camera icon appears on the desktop (Ubuntu example). Mount the camera on a ring stand or tripod over the transilluminator for hands‑free imaging. Perform the imaging in a dark room or cover the setup with a thick, light‑blocking cloth.

steps.title: Launch Entangle and configure capture
steps.instruction: Open the Entangle program. When prompted with "Camera is in use", click Yes to unmount the camera. Activate continuous capture mode by clicking the toolbar button that looks like two stacked rectangles. Turn off the light box, wear orange safety glasses, turn off any overhead lighting, then turn the light box back on. Under camera settings, set exposure time to roughly 1/16–1/8 second (adjust as needed). Capture an image by clicking the camera button; take additional exposures if required, using a slightly brighter exposure because RAW‑to‑TIFF conversion darkens the image.

steps.title: Convert RAW images to TIFF
steps.instruction: If the images are in RAW format (e.g., NEF), convert them to 16‑bit TIFF files.

substeps.instruction: Create a new folder and move all RAW image files into it.
Open a terminal, cd into that folder, and run:

steps.title: Measure band intensities with FIJI
steps.instruction: Analyze the gel image using FIJI (ImageJ).

substeps.instruction: Open the TIFF image (File > Open or drag‑and‑drop).
Select the rectangle tool (top‑left button) and draw a small box around the brightest band. Keep the box size constant for all measurements.
Move the box to each band from left to right (click‑drag or use arrow keys).
Measure each band (Analyze > Measure or Ctrl + M). The Results window will show Area, Mean, Min, and Max values. Repeat for all bands.

steps.title: Export measurement data
steps.instruction: Save the Results table as a comma‑separated values (CSV) file (File > Save As or Ctrl + S) or copy‑paste the values into a spreadsheet.

steps.title: Calculate DNA concentrations
steps.instruction: Use the provided polynomial equation to convert the measured mean fluorescence values into DNA concentrations. If the loading volume of the lambda standards and your genomic DNA samples is identical, no volume correction is needed; otherwise multiply or divide by the appropriate factor. Store genomic DNA in TE buffer, aliquot to avoid multiple freeze‑thaw cycles, keep stock at –20 °C and a working aliquot at 4 °C.

steps.title: Create standard curve and fit polynomial
steps.instruction: In the spreadsheet, highlight the concentration and mean‑fluorescence data, then Insert > Chart. Choose an XY Scatter plot (points only), set data series in columns, and finish. Add a trend line (Insert > Trend Line), select a 2nd‑degree polynomial, and check "Show equation" to display the calibration equation on the chart.

steps.title: Prepare computer for image analysis
steps.instruction: Use a computer with an operating system capable of running the camera control software and FIJI. Linux (Ubuntu 18.04 LTS or later) is recommended; install ImageJ/FIJI (platform‑independent). The protocol was demonstrated on an 8‑year‑old laptop with 8 GB RAM running Ubuntu 18.04 LTS.

description: From the process menu, select subtract background. In the popup window, rolling ball radius should be set at 50 pixels. Click OK. You should see the background signal reduce from the image. Background subtraction can vary quite a bit depending on the image. See the Image J manual for more information https://imagej.nih.gov/ij/docs/guide/146-29.html#sub:Subtract-Background... . Additional information for use in quantifying DNA in agarose gels can be found at https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-45021-6_14 .
